laus.filter: dimensions.survey == LAUS and subject geo:US:county:* and period_type == month

qcew.filter: dimensions.survey == QCEW and dimensions.agglvl_code == 70 (county, total covered, all ownerships) and period_type == annual_average

controls.control_group: not applicable: rankings are scored within each event

estimator.estimand: mean over held-out events of the per-event Spearman correlation between a ranking and the outcome

rankings.exposure: score_i = rank(H_i)/n + lambda * rank(G_i)/n, lambda chosen from {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0} by the highest mean Spearman on development events (ties to the smaller lambda)
rankings.graph: G_i = sum_j w_ij H_j / sum_j w_ij over counties j != i, w_ij = IRS county-to-county migrants i->j plus j->i in 2017-2018 (H_j = 0 outside the candidate set)
rankings.hazard: H_i = max over fixes with wind >= 34 kt of modelled wind V * min(1, (40 km / d)^0.5)
rankings.naive: minus the distance (km) from the county internal point to the nearest fix with wind >= 34 kt

inference.test: one-sided paired sign-flip permutation test across held-out events of mean Spearman(exposure) - mean Spearman(naive) > 0
inference.top_k: top 10% of candidate counties; top-k capture difference reported with the same test

primary.label: seasonally differenced LAUS employment loss: -[(mean ln E(m+1..m+2) - mean ln E(m-2..m-1)) - (same one year earlier)]

placebo_tests.none: a ranking test has no placebo date; the naive ranking is the benchmark

design.question: Given a North Atlantic tropical cyclone's track, does a ranking of US counties built only from pre-event information (modelled wind hazard plus migration-graph proximity to hazard) order the counties by their measured post-event employment loss better than ranking by distance to the track?

treatment.candidate_counties: counties (50 states + DC) whose census_geography internal point is within 300 km of a fix with sustained wind >= 34 kt
treatment.event_month: calendar month of the storm's first fix with wind >= 34 kt within 300 km of any candidate county
treatment.events: storms whose first fix is in 2004-2024 and that have at least 20 candidate counties with outcome data
treatment.source: event_library: library_type tropical_cyclone, basin NA; tracks from the pinned ibtracs version (main track, USA agency wind where reported else WMO)

windows.seasonal_difference: the same window one year earlier is subtracted

assumptions: The realised track is the shock; using it is not look-ahead because the question is 'given this shock, who is reached'.
Migration flows from 2017-2018 precede every held-out event; development events before 2017 use a graph measured after them, which can only affect the choice of lambda, not the held-out score.
LAUS county employment is partly model-based and not seasonally adjusted; the year-earlier difference removes the seasonal pattern but not other shocks in the same months.
A predictive ranking is not an intervention response: the result is labelled predictive_association whichever way it comes out.
identification.estimand: mean over held-out events of the per-event Spearman correlation between a ranking and the outcome
identification.label: predictive_association
identification.meaning: A predictive association scored on held-out events. It says nothing about intervention responses.

results.verdict: On 42 held-out storms (2019-2024) the exposure ranking (lambda=0.0, chosen on 65 development storms) has mean Spearman -0.019 with measured employment loss versus -0.036 for distance to track; difference +0.017, one-sided sign-flip p = 0.189. The pre-registered test fails: the exposure ranking is not shown to beat the naive ranking. This is a predictive association, not an intervention response.
